meta.title: Trial and Reward - deep RL runs (Modules 4-5, episodes 12-19)
meta.machine: Mac Studio, Apple M4 Max, 64 GB; every seed runs single-threaded in its own process, 10 at a time

framework.choice: numpy (hand-written MLP backprop + Adam, gradient-checked: logs/deep_gradcheck.json)
framework.why: For CartPole-sized nets (4-64-64-2, batch 64) a numpy training step is 1.7x faster than PyTorch CPU (1 thread) and 2.7x faster than MLX (CPU); acting on one observation is 2.1x / 5.6x faster (MLX on the GPU: 28x slower per action, and the GPU was busy with the language-model RL job). At SAC's 256-wide nets PyTorch CPU is 1.5x faster per update, but a whole SAC run is under a minute, so one framework (the same as rl_reference.py) everywhere.

meta.seed_policy: Hyperparameters were chosen in pilot runs on seeds 0-5 (logs/pilot/); every reported number comes from fresh seeds 10-14, run once, no seed dropped.
meta.solve_criterion: CartPole-v1 'solved' = mean return of the last 100 training episodes >= 475 (gymnasium reward_threshold); steps_to_solve = total env steps when that first happens.
commands: cd research/experiments && uv venv .venv-deep --python 3.12 && VIRTUAL_ENV=.venv-deep uv pip install gymnasium numpy torch mlx

sac.note: eval = deterministic policy on 10 fixed start states (reset seeds 200000-200009); SAC: 2 tanh(mean)

ppo_pendulum.note: eval = deterministic policy on 10 fixed start states (reset seeds 200000-200009); PPO: clip(mean, -2, 2)

dqn.note: Every 5,000 env steps the greedy policy plays the same 10 start states (reset seeds 100000-100009). q_s0_pred = the network's max_a Q(s0, a); disc_return_actual = sum_t 0.99^t r_t actually collected from s0 (capped by the 500-step limit at 99.34). No policy can be worth more than 1/(1-0.99) = 100.

double_dqn.note: Every 5,000 env steps the greedy policy plays the same 10 start states (reset seeds 100000-100009). q_s0_pred = the network's max_a Q(s0, a); disc_return_actual = sum_t 0.99^t r_t actually collected from s0 (capped by the 500-step limit at 99.34). No policy can be worth more than 1/(1-0.99) = 100.

ppo.note: per PPO update (batch of 512 samples): clip_fraction = share of samples with |ratio - 1| > 0.2, averaged over the update's minibatches (for the no-clip runs nothing is clipped, it measures how far ratios wander); approx_kl = mean((r - 1) - log r) over minibatches; kl_exact_post = exact KL(old || new) over the batch after the update. Consecutive updates averaged to <= 200 points.
